 O R D E R
This criminal original petition has been filed seeking quashment of the FIR in Crime No.454 of 2022 on the file of the 1st respondent police Station.
2.The case of the prosecution in brief:-
The petitioners are husband and wife.
The first petitioner is working as a Manager at Manappuram Gold Finance Limited, Nagercoil Branch.
The 2nd respondent is the Area Manager of the said Manappuram Gold Finance Limited, Nagercoil.

He lodged a complaint that on 03/11/2022, the first petitioner, her aunty and one small boy,
conspired together and taken away gold jewels of 15 packs containing 652.34 grams worth about Rs.30,55,476/-.
Upon the above said occurrence, a case in Crime No.454 of 2022 was registered for the offences under section 120-B, 409, 420 and 381 of IPC.
3.Seeking quashment of the same, these petitioners, who are arrayed as A1 and A2 are before this court.
4.Heard both sides.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD)No.15521 of 2023

5.When the matter was taken up for hearing, on 04/10/2023, the following record of proceedings are made by this court:-
As far as the first petitioner is concerned, she got anticipatory bail only considering her pregnancy at that point of time.
Later, a Questionnaire was issued to her and the same was answered by her and stated that she signed in the document under force and threat.
2.Though the first petitioner has sent a mail with her resignation letter on 02.11.2022, the fact remains that on the date of occurrence, she was working as a Branch Manager.
The overt act attributed against the first petitioner, is a matter for investigation.
Hence, this petition is dismissed in respect of the first petitioner.
She is directed to co-operate with the investigation.
Detailed order will follow.

Ginisha vs The State on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117036814/
2 3.The
Government Advocate (Crl) is directed to inform this Court about the overt act attributed as against the second petitioner.
Post the matter on 01.11.2023.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD)No.15521 of 2023
6.In view of the above said record of proceedings
, the matter was adjourned.
On that date, both were heard with reference to the alleged overt-act attributed against the second petitioner/A2.
With regard to A1, a preliminary observation was made by this court as indicated above.
7.Reading of the CD file further indicates that on the date of the alleged missing of the jewels, the first petitioner/A1 was working as Branch Manager.
On the date itself, she submitted a resignation letter.
That was readily accepted by the Company.
With regard to the missing of the jewels, she was called upon by the Investigating Officer to offer her explanation in the form of questionnaire.

She also submitted her written statement stating that on the particular date of the occurrence, she went out of the branch for securing cash amount leaving the file and other things under the custody of one Arockiya Nishani (Assistant Branch Manager).
Now she has stated that in the explanation that since she has already handed over the charge, after the physical verification of the jewels, she cannot be made responsible.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD)No.15521 of 2023
8.Perusal of the CD file further indicates that the signature of Arockia Nishani is also found to be fake.
Expert opinion is also sought in this regard.
9.When there is a specific allegation that A1 is responsible for the misappropriation, absolutely, I find no reason to quash the proceedings.
Except the fact that she resigned from the Company, no other material fact worth considering is brought on record by the first petitioner.
She has to face the investigation and the trial process.
She is not entitled for quashment of the proceedings and accordingly, this criminal original petition is dismissed.
10.So far as the second petitioner/A2 is concerned, as stated above, who is the husband of the first petitioner, his contention is that he is noway involved in the issue.
Since because, he happened to be the husband of the first petitioner, he has been wrongly roped in this case.
11.Perusal of the CD file shows that money was transferred in the name of the second petitioner/A2.

Apart from that, a clear overt-act has also been attributed against him.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD)No.15521 of 2023 12.When the money was transferred in the account of A2, whether it is a profit of crime or whether the second petitioner/A2 has actually involved in the misuse are all the matters for thorough investigation.
13.On the basis of the FIR, the second petitioner cannot seek the relief of quashment at the initial stage.
The investigation must be taken to its logical conclusion.
